narrative.overview:
The shipped interface makes geographic exploration feel like a calm working atlas: warm ivory surfaces, precise boundaries, plum selection states, and an amber-to-plum map ramp keep the map as the visual center. English labels, compact controls, and an explicit demo-data voice keep the prototype legible while the user moves from national context to a state or county.

The same world is expressed through three complete structures. Explorer pairs one dominant map with a place inspector; Stories adds a narrative rail and a charcoal orbital edition; Compare splits the map into two panes and keeps the comparison explanation and data table visible. All three preserve the same metric library, place search, camera controls, legend, and provenance treatment.

The desktop workspace is held to the viewport above 1100px, with internal inspector and Stories rail scrolling so the map, legend, and footer remain in frame. At mobile widths the app becomes a vertical flow and Compare stacks its panes.
keyCharacteristics: Warm Ember palette with plum emphasis and amber map detail.
Map-first working surface with compact, bordered controls.
Manrope for interface copy and Barlow for numeric/label moments.
Real Census 2017 boundaries with clearly labeled illustrative values.

rules.name: The Honest Index Rule
rules.body: Demo values stay visibly identified as illustrative indexes and are never presented as dollars, people, percentages, or measured statistics.

rules.name: The Ember Ramp Rule
rules.body: Use the warm low-to-dark map ramp for geographic values; reserve plum for selection and actions so the map remains readable.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Keep explanatory interface prose in Manrope and use Barlow only for compact data and label moments that benefit from a tighter measure.

rules.name: The Tonal Surface Rule
rules.body: Keep the map and inspector visually distinct through warm surfaces and thin separators; use shadow mainly for transient or floating layers.

dos: Do keep the map dominant and support it with compact breadcrumbs, controls, legend, and provenance.
Do use Ember Ivory/Panel surfaces, Ember Plum action emphasis, and the existing amber-to-plum map ramp.
Do label synthetic values as illustrative demo indexes and expose source, coverage, period, and unit details.
Do preserve the three shipped structures: Explorer, Stories, and Compare.
Do retain visible keyboard focus treatment and reduced-motion support.
donts: Don't describe demo indexes as real measurements or imply causal relationships in comparisons.
Don't replace the map-first composition with decorative cards or unrelated visual themes.
Don't promote the Stories charcoal/amber variant into the default Explorer palette; it is a documented structure-specific edition.
Don't introduce pill-shaped controls, heavy ornamental shadows, or new font families without evidence from the shipped system.
